propositions: Reopening a closed child does not cascade to its closed parent(s), leaving the data store in an invalid state with a closed parent holding open/in_progress child(ren).

The existing parent-first cascade logic applies only to the open->in_progress edge, but the closed->open edge requires symmetric behavior to maintain the invariant that parents are never more closed than their children.

The cascade decision reads parent status without the write lock, creating a TOCTOU race where a peer can move the parent between the eligibility check and the child's transition; a benign race (parent no longer in eligible status) should allow the child to proceed, matching claim_compute's semantics.
The close-time guard prevents closing a parent with open children, but enforces only one direction; reopening a child can violate the symmetric invariant.
The reopen operation is a thin delegation to transition() that lacks both the cascading behavior and the synchronized error handling that claim and transition already provide.
